[CANON CLOCK — EVENT CALENDAR AND COUNTDOWN RULES]
The Canon Clock is the HUD line that counts down to the next canon event and moves the story forward on its own as time passes. This entry holds the calendar it counts against. Added by @Mazaki.

HOW TO READ THE CALENDAR
- Light-novel anchors: Rudeus lives 407–481 [LN26]; Roa begins in year 414 [LN2]; Nanahoshi is summoned in 417 [LN26]; Rudeus joins the Seven Great Powers in 430 [LN26]; Orsted's loop starts in winter of 330 [LN17].
- Dates use the HUD calendar: K[year], Month 1–12. Rudeus Greyrat is born in K407, Month 1; every canon age follows from that.
- Months are approximate (the novels rarely give exact dates). Keep the ORDER and the YEAR exact; the month only sets the countdown. Once a month is shown in the HUD, keep it consistent.
- "Arc N.P" rows are the canon start points (the same ones the "Start at Arc N.P" command uses). "World event" rows happen to the whole world, whoever is involved.

HUD LINE (Slot 11a, right after Turning Point)
  ⏳ Next Canon Event: [event] — in [N years, N months / N months / N days / this month] (K[year])
  Before K407 (any start with canon on):
  ⏳ Canon Begins: Rudeus Greyrat is born in Buena Village — in [N years, N months] (K407)
  and, when a pre-canon row (Fangs of the Black Wolf era) is still ahead, show it as the Next Canon Event above that line.
  When a Turning Point is nearer than the next event, also show:
  ⚠️ Next Turning Point: [name] — in [time] (K[year])

COUNTING RULES
0. WHICH ROW: the Next Canon Event is always the FIRST calendar row dated AFTER the current HUD date (not the arc's big event, not a row from memory). Count the gap month by month from the two dates: K413 Month 2 → K414 Month 2 = 1 year; K413 Month 4 → K414 Month 2 = 10 months. Copy the row's event name.
1. Recompute the countdown from the HUD date EVERY time the date changes: sleep, travel, training montages, time-skips. Never leave it frozen, never count backwards.
2. The clock runs whether or not {{user}} is anywhere near the event. Distance only changes how and when the news reaches them.
3. When the countdown reaches zero, the event HAPPENS:
   - {{user}} is present or involved: play it out in the scene.
   - {{user}} is elsewhere: it happens off-screen as canon describes (adjusted by any Change, Divergence or earlier choice) and reaches {{user}} later as rumors, letters, refugees or consequences, at believable travel speed.
   - Canon: Join: in the months before the event, roads, jobs and coincidences pull {{user}} toward it; arriving is still their choice.
4. Then advance the Era / Arc line by itself when {{user}} is on a canon story start (Story Arc or Era start, Play as a canon character, Canon: Keep): move it to the arc and start point of the event that just happened, written exactly as "Arc N.P: [Arc Name] — [Start Point]" or "Arc N: [Arc Name]". In Sandbox, update the "(canon: Arc N)" part of the Sandbox line instead. Then retarget the clock to the next row of the calendar.
5. A Turning Point (the Mana Calamity and the like) fires on its date unless {{user}} has directly and believably prevented it in play. Its row is never skipped silently.
6. Canon events that depend on people or choices {{user}} has already changed follow the RIPPLE RULES: if an event lost its cause, drop it from the clock (mark it "averted" once in Active Paths) or move it to its new believable date. Do not force it.
7. Branch Run: keep counting only rows that still make sense in the new history (world events, people who are still on their path). Canon: None: show no clock; only world events that do not depend on Rudeus (none are listed before K417 except the Calamity, which still happens) may appear as "⚠️ Next Turning Point".
8. "Canon Clock: Hidden" in the start command keeps the countdown internal: the GM still tracks it and events still fire, but the HUD line is not shown.

CHECKPOINTS
Canon checkpoints from Changes or Divergences (see CANON MODES) count down on the same clock. When a checkpoint is closer than the next calendar row, it is the one shown in Active Paths with ⚠️; the Canon Clock line keeps showing the next calendar event.

KNOWLEDGE
The clock is a player interface above the HUD wall, like the HUD itself. NPCs never know it. A Native {{user}} does not know the future either; a Reincarnate or Otherworlder only knows what their own life could tell them.
